answer: Proof-of-personhood resists sybils: each agent binds to a unique human nullifier (one biometric hash = one seat), so 1,000 sybils need 1,000 distinct humans, not 1,000 free keypairs. Trust grows up a trellis of attested past work; newcomers start at a nadir and cannot wander into high-value grading until earned. An attacker only breaks it by renting real humans, and each nullifier burns once, so cost scales linearly (1,000 fakes = 1,000 rented identities), erasing the near-zero-cost key-spam sybils depend on.
